about: The tool descriptions as main held them before the ASD-STE100 rewrite (branch explore/full-ste); scripts/ste_check.py compares with them. toolNames: every tool name of this add-on, Agent Link and its other add-ons, to find the ones a text points to.

drawing_make.description: A dimensioned drawing of bodies as an ordinary TechDraw page (template, title block, views, section, dimensions: all TechDraw's own, editable there) laid out in one call, and its SVG, PDF and DXF files. Inputs: bodies [names] (all when left out); views from front, back, top, bottom, right, left, iso (front, top, right, iso when left out); projection first | third (left out: TechDraw's preference, else third with inch units, else first; projectionFrom says which); paper A4 | A3 | auto; scale (0.5 is 1:2; left out, the largest standard scale that fits); dimensions: false leaves the overall sizes off; hidden: true dashes hidden edges; name (the sheet's title); file (a name in the session's folder, or a path; the extension is dropped and the three files share the stem); page: false writes the files only and adds nothing to the document. dims [{ view, kind: length (a, b, along h|v, offset mm) | diameter | radius (a: a round edge), fit "H7" or plus/minus mm, label }] with a and b a point [x, y, z] or a query { body, kind, type, radius, near }; holes: true (every round hole called out where a view sees it end on) or a view's name; holeFits { "6": "H7" }; titleBlock { title, partNumber, revision, material, finish, drawnBy, date, checkedBy, company, generalTolerance } — ask the person for theirs, never make a name up; section: a straight view to draw as a full section, sectionAt mm from the middle towards the viewer, sectionLabel (A). Traps: every call adds a NEW page (and its template, views and dimensions) — object_delete the old page first when redrawing; the PDF and SVG come from TechDraw only with FreeCAD's window up (headless they are Workshop's sheet writer's; filesFrom says which and why); TechDraw works out a view's lines on another thread, so the call waits for them (up to 30 s a view: a detailed assembly takes a while, and a changing tool cannot run as a job); vertex and edge numbers of a view change when the model does, so dimensions are made here, not carried over. Refused: a view that is not one of the seven; a section of iso or of a view not drawn; a scale of 0 or under; dims with a view not drawn or a kind other than length, diameter, radius; holes naming a view not drawn; nothing fits the paper. Reply: files { svg, pdf, dxf paths }, filesFrom, paper, scale ("1:2"), projection, projectionFrom, fill, views [{ view, at, size, scale }], dimensions, section { view, label, plane, cutFaces, cutLineIn }, holes [{ view, diameter, count, label, from, features, calloutOff }], holeTable, calloutsOff, titleBlock, techdrawPage (its label), page { views, viewsReadyIn, viewsNotReady, extentDimensions, extents, dimensions, notOnPage [{ view, type, value, item, why }], template, titleBlock, titleBlockEmptied, section | sectionNote, holeTable, viewsInExport, exportScene, exportSceneAgain, settled { cleared, waited, exportMs, turns, turnMs, seen { changed, recomputed }, late, left } } or pageNote (why there is no page), timing { sheet, page, export { wait, dxf, scene, svg, check, pdf }, settle, turns, turnMs, total }, note, step. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. Behaviour, in full: A drawing of bodies as a normal TechDraw page, editable in TechDraw (its template and title block, its views, section and dimensions), laid out in one call: standard views (front, top, right, iso by default; back, bottom, left too), first-angle (ISO) or third-angle (ASME) projection (left out: TechDraw's own preference, else third angle with inch units, else first; the answer says which and why), at the largest standard scale (1:1, 2:1, 1:2 …) that fits A4 or A3 with room for the dimensions and fills the sheet at most about 70% (the smallest paper at that scale; the iso view at its own scale where it has less room), clear of the template's title block; overall sizes dimensioned once each, outside the views, 10 mm off the outline (dimensions: false leaves them off), hidden: true dashes the hidden edges. Exports SVG, PDF and DXF to the output folder: the page's own TechDraw exports where TechDraw can write them (PDF and SVG need FreeCAD's window), Workshop's sheet writer for the rest (filesFrom says which); page: false writes the files only. dims adds feature dimensions with tolerances or ISO 286 fits (limits written in), holes calls out every round hole, grouped by size and how it is made ("4× ⌀8 THRU ⌴⌀13 ↧8.5"), with a leader in a view that sees it end on (front, right, top …), and lists the ones no drawn view sees end on in a hole table on the sheet; titleBlock fills the template's title block (TechDraw's ISO 5457 template; its sample names and numbers emptied, never a name made up; the date today, the scale and tolerance filled). section: a straight view drawn as a full section (cut square to it through the middle, sectionAt mm towards the viewer; the cut faces hatched, the cutting line lettered sectionLabel, A, in a view that sees it edge on) — for bores, pockets and walls inside. The dims and hole callouts go on the TechDraw page itself as TechDraw's own dimensions, each on its own: one TechDraw cannot take is listed under page.notOnPage by its view and text (item, why), never at the cost of the others or of the overall sizes already listed there. Each overall size is measured by TechDraw between the ends of drawn edges at the view's extremes (never a circle's or arc's centre, which TechDraw also keeps as a vertex), the next pair that measures the size tried if the extremes do not, kept only within 0.05 mm of the part's size. Each hole is found among the view's circles by its radius at the view's scale and its centre as the view projects it about the part's centre (TechDraw centres the part there); a callout whose place matches no circle goes on the view's circle of that size nearest it, with a warning to check it is the hole meant. Every view's lines are worked out (TechDraw does it on another thread) before any dimension goes on it and again before the export: page.viewsReadyIn says how long that took, page.viewsNotReady names any view still not drawn after 30 s; the page is never exported while one is not, and its SVG is checked to hold the views' lines (page.viewsInExport: drawn elements, template's, dimensions, the views' edges, points drawn and the template's; TechDraw writes a view's lines as a few paths of many subpaths each, so the points drawn beyond the template's and an allowance per dimension, at least one per view edge, pass it as well as the elements do), exported once more after a further wait when it does not, and neither SVG nor PDF taken from the page when it still does not (filesFrom says why). After the export the page is left with nothing marked as changed: TechDraw's own exports mark the page's template (drawing it writes its size back) and, on views at any scale but 1:1, its dimensions (the PDF export redraws every view, and a dimension that executes writes its references again), and when a redrawn view's lines are there again — a moment later, on another thread — it recomputes that view's dimensions once more. The call waits for that (page.settled.waited seconds; at most four times what the views took to be drawn and two seconds, 5 s at least, 30 s at most) and takes the mark off where only those writes of TechDraw's own made it (page.settled.cleared, the objects' names), without recomputing anything. page.settled.late names dimensions not seen recomputed again in that time — the next call's health may then still read them as not recomputed yet, and a recompute clears it; page.settled.left [{ object, why }] names what stays marked for a reason of its own (marked before the export, or something else of it changed). Where the call's time went is in the answer, in milliseconds (timing): sheet — Workshop's own projection of the views, the layout and the files' dimensions and callouts; page — the TechDraw page made, the wait for its views' lines among it (page.viewsReadyIn, seconds); export { wait (for the views, before anything is written), dxf, scene (the page's tab shown and painted), svg, check (the SVG read back, once, for the views' lines and the template), pdf (TechDraw's own export, which ends by redrawing every view of the page — that is what the wait afterwards is for, and it cannot be left out of TechDraw's PDF export) }; settle — the wait after the export (page.settled.waited, in ms); turns and turnMs — how many turns of FreeCAD's event loop the whole call ran and the time inside them (a turn runs whatever the window has waiting, not only TechDraw's work: many milliseconds a turn means the window is slow to turn, not the drawing); total. page.settled gives the same for the wait alone (turns, turnMs), exportMs (the export as a whole, as timed round it) and seen { changed, recomputed } (the property writes and recomputes of the document watched from the export's start to the end of the wait). What a drawing with a page costs is the views' lines twice (once for the page, once more after TechDraw's PDF export redraws them) and the exports. Measured on the Mac on a small part: 0.8 s a drawing before the wait after the export was there (run 2); 4.6 and 5.7 s with it (run 3), of which the wait was 0.95 and 1.49 s and the views' first lines 1.15 and 1.03 s where they had taken 0.20 and 0.24 s — the rest was in no field then, which is what timing is for. page: false makes the files only, with no TechDraw and no wait. Before the page's SVG and PDF are exported (TechDraw draws them from the scene of the page's tab, whose views' lines exist only once the tab has been shown and painted), the page is shown as a tab, that tab made the active one and painted, every view asked to repaint (no recompute) and the event loop run; page.exportScene lists the steps done (show, activate, paint, redraw, process), page.exportSceneAgain those before the second export. On the sheet writer's files a hole callout's leader lands only on a drawn circle of the hole's size (within 2%; a thread's tap drill accepted) where the hole projects in that view; a hole with none there (hidden in that view, or drawn otherwise) is left off the sheet, never put on another round edge such as a slot's end or a bore of another size, and listed under calloutsOff (view, label, why) and in its holes row (calloutOff). Hole callouts are kept apart: each one's text (at the sheet's size and at the page's, 3.5 mm, with a margin) clear of the views, the texts and every earlier callout, its leaders crossing no earlier leader nor running through an earlier text, raised 6 mm a try, on either side, at 45, 30 or 60 degrees.

drawing_exploded.description: An assembly manual. steps (required) [{ title, add: [bodies], note }] in the order the parts go together; a body goes in once (a second time is refused, naming its step). Each step is an isometric picture (SVG) with the parts already in place and the new ones moved off by explode mm (left out: 0.6 of the largest size, at least 10), direction up (lifted over their places) or out (away from the middle), a trail to where each goes and a balloon with its item number. Writes the steps and <name>_assembly.md with a bill of materials to the session's folder: bodies of the same shape are one item, with the material and mass where part_spec or material_set recorded one, how each is made from its setup, and Fasteners Workbench hardware by its own name. name: the files' stem; title: the manual's heading. Where every body is in one FreeCAD Assembly this also CHANGES THE DOCUMENT: the moves become the Assembly's own Exploded View (step k's parts k − 1 explode lengths up, or out from step 2 on), editable there, and — unless page: false — an ordinary TechDraw page of it with a balloon per item and the bill of materials. Each call adds another Exploded View and page: delete the old ones (object_delete) before making it again. Outside an Assembly route says the steps use Workshop's own exploded shapes, and — unless page: false — a blank TechDraw page shows the last step's picture as a symbol (pageShows says which step), so the window shows the result; with page: false nothing is added and the call is still one (empty) undo step, so a history_undo straight after it takes back nothing in the document. Trap: each part is lifted over where it is in the document, so put the parts where they go first; warnings names parts that lie apart from the ones before them. Reply: manual (the .md path), steps [{ step, title, adds [{ item, part, qty }], svg }], bom [{ item, part, bodies, size, material, massG, madeBy }], explode, notInAnyStep, warnings, route, routeNote | explodedView, assembly, moves, page | pageNote; outside an Assembly page, pageShows | pageNote. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

patent_figures.description: Patent-style figures FIG. 1 … of bodies (all when left out), one per view (iso, front, top, right when left out; from front, back, top, bottom, right, left, iso): black line art on A4 portrait within the USPTO's margins, no hidden lines or shading, each part's reference numeral (10, 20, 30 … or numerals { "body": n }, the body named by its label or its object's name as bodies takes it, each a whole number over 0 and each its own; the reply's numerals go by label) 3.5 mm high with a lead line to a face of it the viewer sees. A part hidden behind others in a view gets no numeral there (notSeenIn). Writes an SVG and a PDF per figure and a list of the numerals to the session's folder; name is the files' stem and the pages' label. Unless page: false, each figure is also added to the document as an ordinary TechDraw page in that style (blank template, visible lines only, numerals as TechDraw balloons without a bubble), editable in TechDraw — this changes the document, one page a figure, and every call adds new pages (object_delete the old ones first). The files are the page's own exports where TechDraw can write them (FreeCAD's window up), else Workshop's sheet writer's (filesFrom says which and why); page: false writes the files only and changes nothing. After each page's export nothing of it is left marked as changed (TechDraw's export marks the template; as drawing_make, whose description says how); a figure's row carries settled { cleared, waited, exportMs, turns, turnMs, seen, late, left } only when a mark stayed (left), may still arrive after the call (late), or nothing could be watched. Each figure's row always carries timing { sheet, page, export { wait, scene, svg, check, pdf }, settle, turns, turnMs, total } in milliseconds, as drawing_make's (sheet: Workshop's own projection and labels; page: the TechDraw page, its view's lines waited for; export: TechDraw's SVG and PDF and what they need first; settle: the wait after the export; turns and turnMs: the turns of FreeCAD's event loop run for the figure and the time inside them), and the reply timing { figures, turns, turnMs, total } for the whole call. Refused: a view that is not one; a numeral that is not a whole number over 0, used twice, or for a body not drawn. Seconds per figure (exact hidden-line removal), longer for a detailed assembly. Reply: figures [{ fig, view, page | pageNote, svg, pdf, filesFrom, settled, timing }], numerals { label: n }, list (the numerals file), notSeenIn, timing, note. patent_draft uses the numerals and figures of the last call in this session. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

patent_draft.description: A Markdown draft of a patent description and a claims skeleton, written to the session's folder: title (required: what the invention is, a few words), field and background (your words, used as given), bodies (left out: those of the last patent_figures, else all), name (the file's stem). It describes the bodies from the model — their sizes, which adjoin which — with the numerals and figures of the last patent_figures in this session (run that first; without it the draft has no figures or numerals), and leaves in brackets what only the inventor and counsel can say. It is a starting point for a patent attorney's review, marked so in the file: never present it as ready to file, and it is never filed or sent anywhere. Changes nothing in the document. Reply: draft (the path), numerals, figures (how many), adjoining [[a, b] …], note.

library_pack.description: Pack bodies to share as one zip in the session's folder: each body as STEP and STL (formats ["step", "stl"], both when left out; tolerance mm for the STL), a README with their sizes, material and mass and the print settings from their print setup (magnet pauses too), a LICENSE and credits. license (required): CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0 or MIT — ask the person, it decides what others may do with the parts; author is required for all but CC0 (the name they want shown; a handle will do). credits [{ title, author, url, license, changes }] for remixed parts: refused when a credited part's licence does not allow the one chosen (no-derivatives, non-commercial, share-alike). bodies [names] (all when left out); name (the pack's title); description (the README's opening). The STEP header carries the file's name and the author given — no path, user name or organisation; personal names any file that still has one. provider auto (default): ScanRuler-FreeCAD's pack when that add-on is installed (through Agent Link's library_pack service), else Documents' own; provider documents forces Documents' own; by says which made it, serviceNote when the service failed and Documents' made it instead. Refused: no licence or one not listed; no author where the licence needs one; credits that are not a list of objects; formats other than step and stl; no body in the document. Meshing a detailed body for the STL takes a while. Changes nothing in the document. Reply: pack (the zip's path), files, license, parts [{ files, size }], bytes, by, warnings, unsound { bodies, note } (body_check says they are not sound: fix before sharing), personal { files, note }.

kicad_import.description: Read a KiCad board into the document (.kicad_pcb, KiCad 5 to 9; the file is parsed here, KiCad is not needed). path (required): the file's full path. It makes the board as a solid body "PCB <name>" from its Edge.Cuts outline and thickness, with cut-outs and mounting holes through it, and each tall component as a box over its courtyard, a body each. A component's height comes from heights { "J1": mm } given here, else the footprint's STEP model where this computer has it, else a Height property on the footprint; with none known no box is made and noHeight lists the refs. minHeight (3 mm): components under it get no box. centre: true (default) moves the board's middle to the origin (moved says by how much); centre: false keeps KiCad's own coordinates with y turned up. name: the board's name (the file's when left out). The bodies are plain Part solids, and every import adds a new board and components: delete the old ones (object_delete) before importing a changed file. The board's facts (size, holes, footprints, edge connectors, the file's path) are kept with the document for board_enclosure and pcb_order_package. Refused: path is not a file; the file is not a board KiCad 5 to 9 wrote; no closed Edge.Cuts outline. A big board with hundreds of footprints takes several seconds. Reply: board (its label), size [x, y], thickness, copperLayers, holes [{ at, d, kind }], footprints (how many), tall [{ ref, value, side, height, from }], edgeConnectors (what board_enclosure opens the walls for), bodies, noHeight { count, refs, note }, openOutline (pieces of Edge.Cuts that join nothing), moved, step. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

board_enclosure.description: An enclosure round a board that kicad_import read, placed round it where it stands: two new bodies, the box and its lid (the lid laid beside, printed top down — turn it over about X to put it on). board: the board's label (may be left out when one is imported). It puts a standoff under each mounting hole (screw from the hole's size unless screw says M2, M2.5, M3 …), makes the standoff height clear the underside's parts and the headroom the tallest part on top (standoff and headroom mm override), and opens the walls for the edge connectors kicad_import found: skip [refs] leaves some closed, openings [{ side: front|back|left|right, at, width, height, z }] adds more as gen_part's board_box takes them. wall, floor, radius, lid, lip, clearance, gap (board edge to walls) and margin (round each opening), all mm, as board_box's; name: the box's label. Holes take the printer's fit calibration (fit calibrate; 0.2 mm when none is kept, printerFit says). Refused: no board imported yet (kicad_import first; or gen_part { generator: "board_box" } takes the sizes by hand); several boards and none named; a name that is not an imported board; a value out of board_box's range. Each call adds a new box and lid: delete the old pair before making it again. Reply: board, bodies [box, lid], outside [x, y, z], standoff, headroom, standoffs { screw, at, diameter, pilot, pilotDepth }, openings [{ …, for: the connector's ref or "given" }], printerFit, sound { label: true|false }, openingHeightGuessed { refs, mm, note } (connectors with no known height got a 5 mm opening: give heights in kicad_import), step. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

pcb_order_package.description: Package a board's fabrication files for ordering; nothing is uploaded, ordered or paid for — that is the person's to do. files (required): full paths of the Gerbers, drill files, BOM and placement (CPL) files KiCad's fabrication outputs wrote; they are sorted by kind. vendor jlcpcb | pcbway | oshpark (the order sheet says what to upload where for that house). The board's size comes from board (an imported board's label), else size [x, y] mm, else it is read from the outline Gerber; layers (copper), thickness mm, quantity; name: the files' stem. Writes to the session's folder: <name>_gerbers.zip (upload-ready), <name>_order.zip (that, the assembly files and the order sheet) and <name>_ORDER.md. When kicad-cli is on this computer's PATH it runs KiCad's design rule check on kicadPcb (a .kicad_pcb path; else the imported board's own file) and reports it under drc { errors, warnings, unconnected, first }; otherwise drc says why it was not run — an order is not checked until it is. Refused: a path in files that is not a file; no Gerber among them; an unknown vendor; a board that was not imported. Changes nothing in the document. Reply: gerberZip, package, orderSheet (paths), vendor, board { size, layers, thickness }, files { kind: how many }, drc, warnings, note.

printed_channel.description: Cut a channel inside a body along a path for a wire or a conductive trace. path (required): [[x, y, z] …], two or more points in document coordinates, each at least the section's size from the one before; an end on the part's face opens there (it is carried 1 mm past the face), an end inside stops blind; between its ends the channel must stay inside the part. section { shape: round | square, size: 0.4 to 20 mm (the diameter or side; 2 when left out) }; corners are rounded to bend mm (the section's size or 2, whichever is more); a turn of over 170° is refused. fill: wire (default: the channel takes the printer's hole calibration; awg 10 to 40, 22 when left out, gives the wire's diameter, whether it fits with 0.4 mm to spare, and its copper resistance), filament (also makes the trace as its own body "<body> trace" for a second material unless trace: false; resistance from material carbon-pla | electrifi or resistivity Ω·cm), or paint (resistance the same way). The channel is written into the body as a plain shape, so the body must be a plain Part solid (Part::Feature — an enclosure from board_enclosure or gen_part, an import, a part_transform copy): a PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object is refused, naming the plain copy to make, because FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the channel. Refused too: the sweep fails (fewer, longer segments or a larger bend), the channel cuts nothing (the path is outside the part), or it leaves the part unsound (move the path off the faces it grazes). Face and edge numbers of the body change. Reply: body, bodies (the trace too), length mm, section { shape, size, areaMm2 }, ends [open | blind, …], bend, removed mm³, sound, conductor { fill, resistivityOhmCm, ohms, note, wire { awg, diameter, ohms, channelAtLeast, fits, note } }, printerFit, step. A printed trace reads several times higher across layers than the figure given. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

fastener_types.description: Fasteners Workbench's types, sizes and lengths, read from its own tables (these tools are listed only when Fasteners Workbench is installed). Three levels: no type → the types that match query (words, all must match: "socket cap"), standard (ISO, DIN, ASME …) and kind (screw, nut, washer, insert, pin …): count and types [{ type, kind, what }] (the first 40; narrow the query for more); type ("ISO4762") → that type's sizes ["M3", …] and hasLength; type and size → lengths (the lengths it comes in, or length { any, default } for one cut to length), hole (the pass and tap hole diameters from Fasteners' own screw calculator) and insert (an IUT heat-set insert's hole and depth). A type that is not one is refused not_found with the nearest names; a size the type does not come in, with those it does. Sizes are written as Fasteners writes them (M3, #10, 1/4in). Changes nothing. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.

fastener_add.description: Add a Fasteners Workbench part (screw, bolt, nut, washer, insert, pin …). type (required): Fasteners' type name, e.g. ISO4762 (fastener_types { query } finds one). edges: round edges to attach one fastener to each — "Plate.Edge7", or { body, near: [x, y, z] } with a point on the round edge or at the hole's centre (within 1 mm; at a centre the nearest centre wins, then the hole's outer rim). Prefer near: edge numbers change after any edit of the body. Without edges it is made loose at at [x, y, z] (the origin when left out). size (M3; it wins over the hole; left out on edges, Fasteners matches it to the edge's diameter); length mm (the nearest length the type comes in); thread simple (a plain cylinder: fast, the default) or real (a modelled thread: slow and heavy, for close-ups only); match outer (the edge is a pass hole: the screw goes through; default) or inner (a tap hole: its thread fits it); invert: true turns it end for end; offset mm along its axis. On an edge it is seated: its head (a nut's or washer's face, an insert's top) on the open side of the edge and the shank into the material, whichever way FreeCAD's circle for that edge points (Fasteners puts the head where the circle's axis points, and on a PartDesign Hole that can be into the plate); invert: true turns it end for end from seated. Where the shape cannot tell the open side (a rim with material on both sides) it is as Fasteners places it. A size given on a counterbore's wall goes on the bore's edge at its floor, and attachNote says so. Kept on its hole: each attached fastener also remembers the edge's geometry (centre, axis, radius), so when a later PartDesign feature renumbers the Body's edges it is put back on the same round edge (reattached); when no edge of that size is left within reach it stays where it is and says so (lost, and a Report-view warning) — fastener_set { edge } puts it on another. Labels read "M8x25-Screw", "M8x25-Screw 2" …, numbered per size and kept (Fasteners itself relabels at every recompute). Refused: an unknown type (nearest names given), a size the type does not come in, an edge that is not circular or a point with no round edge within 1 mm (the nearest are listed), thread or match other than their two words. Reply: made [{ object, label, type, kind, size, length, thread (simple | real), matchOuter, invert (Fasteners' own Invert), offset, attachedTo ("Plate.Edge7"), edgeDiameter, headSide (open side, or in the material when turned end for end), shankOut (mm the shank stands out of the hole's far rim: a screw longer than its hole), at, bom (its BOM line), hidden, attachNote, hole (kept | reattached | lost), reattached, lost, adopted }], source. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.

fastener_set.description: Change Fasteners parts in place, as Fasteners' own Change Parameters, Flip and Move do; each keeps its object name and label. objects (required unless only restore): names or labels (fastener_list gives them). Give any of: type (only one with the same properties: a screw to another screw standard; refused otherwise, listing what it can become), size ("Auto": matched to its hole again), length mm (the nearest it comes in), thread simple | real, invert (true: turned end for end from seated, its head into the material; false: seated, head on the open side), offset mm, match inner | outer, edge ("Plate.Edge9": move it to another round edge, seated there, turned end for end only when it was or invert says so), label (for ONE fastener: the label it then keeps across recomputes; with several objects it is refused). restore: true gives the document's Fasteners objects their behaviour back when the file was saved where Fasteners Workbench was not loaded (alone it needs no objects; reply restored). Refused: no objects, an object that is not a Fasteners part, a type it cannot become, a size it does not come in. Reply: changed [{ object, label, type, kind, size, length, thread (simple | real), matchOuter, invert (Fasteners' own Invert), offset, attachedTo ("Plate.Edge7"), edgeDiameter, headSide (open side, or in the material when turned end for end), shankOut (mm the shank stands out of the hole's far rim: a length longer than the hole, as a 20 mm screw in a 10 mm plate), at, bom (its BOM line), hidden, attachNote, hole (kept | reattached | lost), reattached, lost, adopted }]. A fastener the call changed that is still "not recomputed yet" after its last step (and was not before the call) is recomputed once more, so the next call's health check does not list it. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.

fastener_list.description: The Fasteners parts in the document and their bill of materials, counted from the objects as they are now: fasteners [{ object, label, type, kind, size, length, thread (simple | real), matchOuter, invert, offset, attachedTo ("Plate.Edge7"), edgeDiameter, at, bom (its BOM line), hidden, attachNote, hole (kept | reattached | lost), reattached, lost, adopted }] and bom [{ item ("ISO4762 Screw M3x12"), qty }], each fastener once, hidden ones too (hidden: true), plus the links and arrays of it Fasteners counts. Before listing, each attached fastener is checked against its hole: hole kept, reattached (put back on the same circle after FreeCAD renumbered the edges) or lost (its hole moved or was removed; also under warnings — fastener_set { edge } puts it on one). Fasteners from before Workshop kept them (older documents, or added with Fasteners' own buttons) are taken in as the document opens or recomputes: their hole from the edge they are on, a label Fasteners counted up put back in the per-size scheme; adopted: true says so. sheet: true also puts the BOM in a spreadsheet in the document (Fasteners' own Generate BOM with the window up, else Workshop's in the same layout): that call changes the document and the reply adds sheet and by. Without sheet it is a read (the reattaching above is the keeper's own doing, not this call's). Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.

fastener_print.description: Fasteners Workbench's 3D-print thread settings (its own preference, for every document on this computer — not kept with the file). Called with nothing it only reads them: mode (standard | 3dprint), nut [A, B], screw [A, B], formula, source. A printed thread's diameter is d x A + B: nut for inside threads (1.03, 0.1 to start), screw for outside ones (0.99, −0.05); they apply when mode is 3dprint. Give mode, nut [A, B] and/or screw [A, B] to set them: every fastener with a real (modelled) thread in every open document is then recomputed and named under redone — slow when there are many. Refused: a mode other than the two; nut or screw that is not two numbers. thread_cut's modelled threads in a printed body take the nut figures as their clearance when mode is 3dprint. Not undone by history_undo: it is a preference, not part of the document; call it again with the old figures. Fasteners Workbench: Shai Seger; screw_maker: Ulrich Brammer.

fit.description: Sizes for parts that fit together, and the printer's fit calibration. action (size when left out): size { nominal mm (the bought or mating part's size), of: hole|shaft (hole when left out), kind: press|snug|slide|free (all four when left out), body } gives the diameter to MODEL: a hole is nominal + the fit's gap + what this printer prints a hole small; a shaft is nominal − what it prints a peg big (the fit's gap is always put on the hole). calibrate { hole, shaft } keeps how much this printer prints a hole small and a peg big (diametral mm, each −1 to 1; hole 0.2 and shaft 0 when left out) with the document: every later size, hw_hole and hw_embed takes it. stack { items: [{ name, nominal (signed mm), tol (± mm) }], target: [lo, hi] } adds a tolerance stack. Gotchas: with no calibration kept the hole allowance is 0.2 mm and printerFit says so; a body's print setup's own fit wins over the document's (body picks the setup). calibrate writes a record though the tool is listed as a read: it is not an undo step. Reply: size { of, nominal, model { kind: mm }, printerFit }; calibrate { calibration { hole, shaft }, note }; stack { nominal, worstCase [lo, hi], rss [lo, hi], worstCaseOk, rssOk (with target) }.

hw_hole.description: A hole for hardware in a body: kind clearance | counterbore | countersink | nut_trap (size M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5, M6 or M8; M3 when left out; fit close|normal|loose is ISO 273 fine|medium|coarse), insert (heat-set, same sizes) or magnet (size "6x2": diameter x thickness mm). at [x, y, z] in document coordinates is where it ENTERS, on a flat face; dir runs INTO the material ("-z" when left out; "+x", "-y" … or [x, y, z]); depth mm or "through" (the default; insert and magnet pockets take their own depth). The head side (screw head, counterbore, countersink, nut trap) is always on the face at is on: headSide says which ("countersink on the face at x=0, facing -x"); for a wall bracket enter from the face away from the wall. In a PartDesign Body it is FreeCAD's own PartDesign Hole on a new sketch on that face (features lists them: HoleSketch, Hole, and NutTrapSketch + NutTrap, a Pocket, for a nut trap), editable in its panel. face: the entry face instead of finding it from at and dir — "Face6" (on the Body's tip) or "Pocket.Face4" (a feature's); face numbers change after any edit, so pick it again (shape_query) rather than reuse one. sketch: a sketch in the Body whose circles' centres are the holes (at not needed; not for nut_trap). Printer allowance: the print setup's or the document's fit calibration (fit calibrate), 0.2 mm when none is kept, is added to the diameters. With an allowance the Hole is FreeCAD's plain hole (ThreadType None) at the ISO 273 size + allowance, because FreeCAD sets a sized hole's Diameter again from size and fit on every reopen; the size it stands for is in the Hole's Label2 and allowanceOn names the properties. A size picked later in the Hole's own panel loses the allowance: run hw_hole again instead. Other bodies: a plain Part solid (Part::Feature) is cut as a shape (route "Part solid", not editable); a parametric Part object (a Part::Box, a boolean, an extrusion) is refused, because FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the hole — the refusal names the plain copy (part_transform copy) or pd_clone to use. The Body is recomputed first; a broken last feature is refused by name. Each call is one hole (or one sketch's holes). Reply: body, kind, size, sizes (freecadSize, fit, clearance, clearanceBeforeAllowance, cut, cutDiameter, cutDepth, nutAcrossFlats, nutDepth, hole, depth — those that apply), printerFit, allowance, depth, through (mm of material passed), removed (mm³), route ("PartDesign Hole" | "Part solid"), features, headSide (+ face, facing), note, sound (+ problems), step. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. More: guide_read { topic: "hole" }.

thread_lookup.description: Thread sizes in mm, read from FreeCAD's own PartDesign Hole tables (ISO metric coarse and fine, UNC, UNF) once a session. size ("M6", "M10x1.25", "1/4-20", "#10-32"; a bare "1/4" is the coarse one) gives thread { size, series, major, pitch, pitchDia, minorInt, minorExt, tapDrill, freecad (the name FreeCAD's Hole lists it by), source, insert { hole, depth, source } where there are heat-set insert figures, tpi and tapDrillName for Unified sizes }. Without size: a table for series metric | metric-fine | unc | unf | all (all when left out); near: a diameter mm keeps the six sizes whose major is nearest. Reply then threads [{ size, major, pitch, minorInt, tapDrill }], columns, source. Gotchas: pitch diameter and minors are worked out from the ISO 68-1 basic profile, not read from FreeCAD; FreeCAD gives no Unified pitch, so a Unified size FreeCAD lists but Workshop has no threads-per-inch for has pitch null. A size that is not listed is refused not_found; your own sizes go in ~/.config/workshop_make/threads.json. Changes nothing.

thread_identify.description: What thread a hole or shaft is. faces: the cylindrical wall by query — { near: [x, y, z] } (a point on or beside it; only cylindrical faces are looked at) or { faces: ["Face7"] } (face numbers change after any edit); body when there is more than one. Reply: body, face, diameter, kind (hole | shaft), length, axis, nearest [{ size, series, pitch, as (a hole read as tapDrill, minor or major; a shaft as major), standard, off (mm from it) }], best, alsoPicked. When sizes tie but for pitch (M10, M10x1.25, M10x1) the reply has needs: "pitch" and ask instead of best: ask the person or measure, then call again with pitch mm. A note says when the nearest is over 0.3 mm off (a clearance hole, a press fit, not a thread). scan: { axis: { element } | { origin, direction, radius }, band, length, pitchFloor } reads a scanned thread instead (pitch, starts, hand, flank, the standard it matches; families narrows them) — only with ScanRuler-FreeCAD installed (its scan_thread), else refused unavailable. Changes nothing; thread_cut threads the hole.

thread_cut.description: Thread an existing hole with FreeCAD's PartDesign Hole. faces (required): the hole's cylindrical wall, { near: [x, y, z] } or { faces: ["Face7"] } (numbers change after any edit); size ("M6", "M10x1.25", "1/4-20"; left out, the nearest standard size — refused when two sizes fit alike or none is within 0.3 mm); mode cosmetic (default: the hole drilled to the tapping size, the thread recorded with the document, tap it after making) or modelled (the helix cut into the part: slow, a second or more per turn, and many faces afterwards — keep it for coarse threads that will be printed, M5 and up); depth mm (the hole's length when left out); from [x, y, z]: which end to start at (the open end, the upper one of two, when left out). In a PartDesign Body the thread is a real feature that stays: a sketch at the hole's end (ThreadSketch) and a PartDesign Hole (Thread, Threaded, ModelThread for modelled), editable in the Hole's panel; route "PartDesign Hole", features names them. In a plain Part solid (Part::Feature) the Hole is made in a scratch Body and the result written back as a plain shape (route "Part solid"); a parametric Part object (Part::Box, a boolean …) is refused, since FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the thread — the refusal names the plain copy or pd_clone. A shaft (outside thread) is recorded cosmetic only: FreeCAD threads holes, not shafts. Refused when the hole is already over the thread's major diameter, or the size is one of your own that FreeCAD's Hole does not list. A modelled thread in a body in a print setup takes Fasteners Workbench's 3D-print clearance when that is installed (printClearance). Reply: thread { body, size, series, mode, kind, diameter, depth, at, into, holeDiameter, feature }, removed (mm³), sound (+ problems), route, features, step, note, warning (modelled under M5 in a print), warning2 (the hole was wider than the tap drill). A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

hw_embed.description: Encase a bought part mid-print: cut a closed pocket for it inside a body that is in a print setup, and record the pause to drop it in. kind nut (size M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8), magnet ("6x2": diameter x thickness), bearing (623, 624, 625, 626, 608, 688, 6000, 6001, MR105, MR85, or "22x7": outer diameter x width), insert (M2…M8), weight (size "20x8" round or "30x20x6" box, or dims), box (dims [w, d, h]) or cylinder (dims [diameter, h]). at [x, y, z] (required, document coordinates): the centre of the pocket's FLOOR, inside the material; the part stands upright (+z), turn ° about z. fit press|snug|slide|free (slide: drops in by hand) with the printer's fit calibration; headroom mm over the part (0.2); the pocket's top is rounded up to the setup's layer grid and the pause comes after that layer. Refused: no print setup (setup add first); the pocket would come out of the part; no material over it (use hw_hole for a pocket pressed in after); the roof is under 2 layers or minRoof mm. The pocket is written into the body as a plain shape, so the body must be a plain Part solid (Part::Feature — gen_make's, an import, a part_transform copy): a PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object is refused, naming the plain copy to make, because FreeCAD would rebuild it and lose the pocket. Trap: the part goes in from above, so nothing may overhang the pocket at the pause; +z is the print direction. Reply: body, id (E1 …), what, pocket { shape, size, depth, floor, top (mm from the bed) }, pause { afterLayer, z, note }, roof, least { roof, wall }, sides (least wall beside or under it), printerFit, step, warning when sides is under the least wall. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. More: guide_read { topic: "embed" }.

hw_embed_list.description: The parts encased in a body (hw_embed's records): embeds [{ id, what, pocket (its sizes mm), floor and top (mm from the bed), layer (the pause comes after it), roof (mm of material over it), note }]. A record whose pocket is solid again (an undo, or a later edit filled it) is dropped from the list and named under dropped { ids, why }. body may be left out when there is one. Reads; only the dropping of dead records is written.

hw_unembed.description: Take an encased part out again by its id (hw_embed_list gives them): the pocket is filled back to solid and its pause dropped; keepPocket: true leaves the pocket as an open hole (the part pressed in after printing) and drops only the pause. Filling writes a plain shape, so as with hw_embed the body must be a plain Part solid. An id that is not there is refused, listing those that are. Reply: body, removed (the id), pocket ("filled" | "left open …"), solids, step. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

hw_pauses.description: Every pause a body's print needs, on its print setup's layer grid: pauses [{ afterLayer (1 is the first layer), z (mm from the bed: the top of that layer), ids, note (what goes in), merged (two on one layer made one) }], count, layerHeight, firstLayer. Counts hw_embed's pockets and gen_make's magnets (id gen_make); mass_ballast's pockets are not in this list (its own reply gives pauseAt). Refused when the body is in no print setup. slice and slice_with write these pauses into the G-code. Changes nothing but dropping records whose pocket is gone (dropped).

setup.description: How each part is made, recorded with the document (a hidden records object, saved in the .FCStd and undone with the rest). action (list when left out): list → setups [{ id (S1 …), type, name, bodies, its settings }] and types (each type's settings, explained); of { body } → that body's setup or none; add { type: print|cut|mill, bodies: [names], settings, name } → added; set { id (or the setup's name), bodies (replaces the list) | add: [names] | remove: [names], settings (a value of null drops that setting), name } → setup; remove { id } → removed. Print settings: printer (generic, bed-slinger, corexy, h2d), nozzle mm, layerHeight, firstLayer, walls, infill %, topLayers, bottomLayers (up is +z only; slicerPresets is set by slicer_presets use). Cut: machine (laser, waterjet, plasma, router), thickness, kerf, material, sheet [w, h]. Mill: axes "3" | "3+2", minTool, grade (IT 5–14), directions, material, stock [x, y, z], reach. Gotchas: a body is in at most one setup of a type (add refuses it, naming the setup set { remove } to run first); bodies are recorded by Label, so a body renamed afterwards drops out of its setup — set { add } it again; an unknown setting is refused with the list. A body in no setup has no process: nothing here guesses one — ask the person, then add. dfm_check, slice, hw_embed, cut_check and mill_check read the setup. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

part_spec.description: The limits every part of this document must meet, and what parts are made of; kept with the document. spec { minWall mm, massMin g, massMax g, minSafety (a safety factor, judged against the last fea_solve), minClearance mm }: each given key is set, null drops it, clear: true starts from none; anything else is refused. Called with nothing it answers what is kept. material: a printing filament id (pla, petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a) for bodies [names] (the one body when left out), "" forgets theirs; it also puts FreeCAD's own material card on the body where one matches (freecadMaterial). For any other material (metals, woods, FreeCAD's library) use material_set. Gotchas: the spec is one for the whole document, not per body; materials are kept by body Label. Reply: spec, materials { label: id }, freecadMaterial { label: { card } | { note } }. part_review judges a body against the spec. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

dfm_check.description: Is a body printable as it stands, +z up, with its print setup's nozzle and printer (a 0.4 mm nozzle on a generic printer when it is in no setup): thin walls (under one line an error, under two lines or 0.8 mm a warning), overhangs past 50° from vertical, flat ceilings over 10 mm (bridges), upright holes too small to print open, too little bed contact, tall and thin (over 8:1), over the build volume, and FreeCAD's Check Geometry. Reply: body, setup, verdict, findings [{ id (F1 …, worst first), rule (thin-wall, overhang, bridge, small-hole, bed-contact, tall-thin, build-volume, check-geometry), severity, value, limit, unit, at [x, y, z], areaMm2, says (what to do), waived }], wall { least mm, at, read (how many rays), by }, rules (the limits used). waive { id, reason } accepts one finding of the LAST dfm_check of that body on purpose (run the check first; ids are per check): it is kept with the document and that rule at that place comes back waived from then on. Heavy on detailed bodies (rays against every face): it runs as a job when long — a reply with a job id is finished with job_status. Walls are sampled by rays, so a thin spot between samples can be missed; view_render can draw the wall map (view_maps lists the maps). Listed as a read: waive writes its record without an undo step. part_review folds this check into one verdict. verdict: the check in a few words from the findings not waived ("printable", "printable, 2 warnings", "not printable: 1 problem, 1 warning"), the words Agent Link's Activity tab and caption show for the call.

part_review.description: One verdict on a part — pass, fix or unknown — to run after every change. It checks soundness (one valid closed solid), then what its setup decides: in a print setup the printability check's findings count; in no setup they come under ifPrinted for information; in a cut or mill setup they are skipped (cut_check, mill_check judge those). The least wall and the mass (as printed in a print setup: walls, skins and infill, an estimate; encased magnets, ballast and embeds counted) are judged against the spec kept by part_spec, or spec { minWall, massMin, massMax } given here for this review only; minSafety is judged against the last fea_solve of this body if it is not stale. material: an id for this review only (the body's own, else PLA). waive: [{ rule, at [x, y, z], reason }] accepts a place on purpose (kept; written without an undo step). Reply: body, process (printed | cut | mill | unknown), processFrom, verdict, findings [{ source, severity, says, at }] (the first 8, errors first), figures { volume, mass, material, as, encasedMass, safety, wall }, checks (what ran or was skipped and why), spec, ifPrinted, unjudged (limits that could not be judged — these make the verdict unknown), printing { pauses }. Heavy on detailed bodies: it runs as a job when long (job_status finishes it). unknown is not pass: read unjudged and supply what is missing.

slice.description: Slice a body that is in a print setup with the slicer on this computer and write G-code to the session's folder. With the person's presets on the setup (slicer_presets use) their slicer slices it (as slice_with); otherwise PrusaSlicer's command line with the setup's layer height, nozzle, walls and infill (AGENTLINK_SLICER names another binary), or, when PrusaSlicer is absent, whichever of OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio is here (note says so). Needs Agent Link for OrcaSlicer installed (it holds the slicers' command lines); refused unavailable, saying how to get it, when it is not. settings { … } overrides the setup's for this slice; name: the file's base name (the body's label when left out); pauseCommand (M601) is written before the first layer over each encased part (hw_embed, gen_make's magnets). material: a filament id (pla, petg, abs, asa, pa6-cf, tpu-95a) for this slice only, not recorded; left out, the body's own. Refused: the body is in no print setup (the refusal gives the setup add call); its material is not a printing filament (a metal, a wood), naming material_set and the one-off material. The body is meshed at 0.01 mm deviation first: seconds for a simple part, a minute or more and a large STL for a detailed one; it runs as a job when long (job_status). Reply: body, slicer, gcode (path), bytes, time, filament (g, mm) and layers as the slicer reports them, verdict (a few words: its time and filament, "12m 3s, 3.21 g", else "G-code written"), setup, pauses, material (when given), note. Starting a print is the person's call (printer_send).

mass_calibrate.description: Calibrate mass to a weighed print: grams (what the finished print weighed, anything encased in it included) for a body. Every later mass reading for bodies in the same print setup — or, for a body in no print setup, of the same material — is scaled to match (mass_properties, mass_target, mass_ballast). Kept with the document; reset: true drops it. Refused when grams is missing or under what is encased, or the weight is under 0.3 or over 3 times the estimate (not the same part and settings: check the body, its setup and its material). Reply: calibrated (the key: setup:S1 or solid:<material>), scale, expected (g, before), weighed, encased, for, note; reset answers reset and was. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

mass_properties.description: Mass, centre of mass and inertia of each body (body, or every body shown when left out) in its material: as printed when it is in a print setup (walls, top and bottom skins and infill — an estimate; the slicer's figure from slice is closer), else solid. Encased parts are counted: gen_make's magnets, ballast cut by mass_ballast, and a calibration from mass_calibrate is applied. A body with no material is taken as PLA and says so (material_set or part_spec { material } gives it one). Reply: bodies [{ body, mass g, com [x, y, z] mm, volume mm³, material, materialId, density g/cm³, as (how it was weighed), inertia { aboutCom 3x3 g·mm², principal }, encased [{ what, count, mass }], bodyMass }], units, hardware (Fasteners Workbench screws, listed apart in steel), note, printedNote. Coordinates are the document's. Changes nothing.

mass_target.description: How far a body is from a target: mass g (over 0) and/or com [x, y, z] mm with null for an axis that does not matter (e.g. [null, null, 10]). At least one is needed. massTol g and comTol mm (0.5 each) decide met. Reply: body, now { mass, com }, mass { target, off, offPct }, com { target, off, distance }, met, and what would get there: ballast { mass, centre (where one ballast's centre must sit to meet both), insideBody, note } when it is too light, remove { mass } when it is too heavy (ballast only adds), or moment { needed g·mm } when only the centre is off. Mass is as mass_properties weighs it (as printed in a print setup). Changes nothing; mass_ballast lays the pockets out.

mass_ballast.description: Lay out closed, upright (+z) round ballast pockets inside a body to reach a target mass g and/or move the centre of mass (com [x, y, z], null for a free axis); at least one is needed. fill steel-bb (7.85), lead (11.3), tungsten (18) or a density in g/cm³; packing: the share of a pocket the fill takes, 0.1–1 (0.6 loose shot, 1 a cast slug); diameter mm (8, at least 2); minWall mm kept clear of every surface (the spec's minWall, else 1.2; at least 0.4); maxPockets (12). Without cut it only plans (cut: false in the reply, nothing changed): read the plan, then call again with cut: true to cut them in one undo step; the fill is then counted by mass_properties. cut writes a plain shape, so the body must be a plain Part solid (Part::Feature): a PartDesign Body or a parametric Part object is refused, naming the plain copy to make. Refused: the body already weighs the target or more; the fill is no denser than the part as made; no room for a pocket (smaller diameter or wall); over 600 places to try (a larger diameter). Cost: every candidate place is probed up the body's height and then checked whole against the body, a few seconds on a detailed body; cut: true took 26 s on a plate with ten pockets (it weighs the cut body as printed). The pockets are searched greedily: massOff and comOff say how close it got, it is not always exact. Reply: body, fill { what, density, packing, pocketDensity }, pockets [{ at (the floor's centre), diameter, depth, fill g }], before and after { mass, com }, fillMass, minWall, leftOut { places, why } (places not used because a hole or pocket of the part runs through the pocket or its wall there: each pocket and its wall is checked to be all material), massOff, comOff, printing { pauseAt mm, note } (pause there, fill, print over — hw_pauses does not list it), cut, sound, step, next. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

slicer_presets.description: The person's own slicer presets, as data. slicer bambustudio (default) | orcaslicer. action (list when left out): list { slicer, kind: machine|process|filament, query, limit } → the presets on this computer by kind, each kind { count (all of that kind that match), own (how many are the person's own), presets (the person's own first, each { name, own: true }, then the names of the others, limit of them: 10 when neither kind nor query is given, else 50; 0 gives the counts and the person's own only), more (how many are not shown: kind, query or a higher limit, up to 500, shows them; nothing is out of reach) }, and saved bundles; from (the preset folders read) and next are given on the first list of each slicer in a session and again when the folders change, else named in saidBefore; fetch { slicer: "orcaslicer", vendors: ["BBL", "Prusa" …], version } downloads OrcaSlicer's system presets of the same version as JSON (it needs the network; OrcaSlicer packs its own where they cannot be read); use { body, machine, process, filament } (names from list) or { body, bundle } puts them on the body's print setup: its layer height, walls, infill and shells then come from the presets (settingsFromPresets) and slice uses them — this writes the setup; export { machine, process, filament | bundle | body, path, name } writes one flattened JSON bundle and keeps it; import { path, name } keeps a bundle from a file. Needs Agent Link for OrcaSlicer installed. PrusaSlicer has no presets here: give slice_with profiles { config: an .ini }. Refused: no presets of that slicer on this computer; a name that is not found; use on a body in no print setup. Nothing of any printer is in the code: the presets are the authority. Reply by action: list { slicer, from, the presets by kind { count, own, presets, more }, saved, next, note, saidBefore }; use { setup, presets, slicer, settingsFromPresets, note }; export { exported (path), name, presets }; import { imported, kept, presets, next }.

slice_with.description: Slice a body in a print setup with a named slicer by its command line: slicer prusaslicer (default), orcaslicer or bambustudio. profiles: { machine, process, filament } JSON file paths for OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio, { config } an .ini for PrusaSlicer; left out, the setup's presets (slicer_presets use) or else minimal profiles written from the setup (the slicer's defaults for the rest: fine for a time and weight estimate, not for a real print). OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio also take bodies [names] (several on one plate, arranged), orient and arrange (the slicer's own), overrides { the slicer's process keys }, and project: true (the sliced plate as a .3mf its window opens; slice_open shows it). material: a filament id for this slice only, not recorded (a filament profile or the setup's presets win over it). name: the files' base name. Pauses for encased parts (hw_embed, gen_make's magnets) are written after their layer — M601, Bambu's M400 U1, or pauseCommand — but not with several bodies or orient (the heights are one body's as modelled); warning says when one could not be placed. Refused: no print setup; the setup's presets belong to another slicer; a profile path that is not a file; orient, arrange, project, overrides or several bodies with prusaslicer; a slicer not on this computer (unavailable, naming those present; AGENTLINK_ORCASLICER and AGENTLINK_BAMBUSTUDIO set their paths). Needs Agent Link for OrcaSlicer installed. Cost: the body is meshed at 0.01 mm deviation, then the slicer runs — from seconds to minutes; it runs as a job when long (job_status finishes it). Reply: body, slicer, exe, profiles (which were used), gcode (path), bytes, time, filament and layers as read from the G-code, verdict (a few words: its time and filament, "12m 3s, 3.21 g", else "G-code written"), setup, the slicer's warnings and plate statistics, bodies, project, pauses, pauseCommand, material, overrides, note. Starting the print is the person's call.

slice_read.description: Read an OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio project (.3mf) back — one slice_with wrote (project: true), or one the person changed and saved in the slicer's window. path: absolute, or relative to the session's folder. Reply: the slicer, the presets it names and each setting changed from them (project-wide and per filament), every object's own settings and modifier parts, the plates, the slicer's warnings, and when it holds a sliced plate its time, weight, cost and features. slice: true first slices the project as it stands (its own settings, headless; seconds to minutes) and adds slicedNow { gcode, time, filament … }. Refused: no such file; not a slicer project; the slicer is not on this computer. Changes nothing in the document: to take a changed setting into the print setup, use slicer_presets or setup set.

slice_open.description: Open a project (.3mf; path absolute or relative to the session's folder) in the slicer's own window for the person: slicer orcaslicer (default) or bambustudio. They change what they like there and save; slice_read then brings it back. It only starts the slicer and answers at once — it does not wait for the person or know when they are done: ask them. Needs the FreeCAD window (refused headless) and the slicer on this computer. Reply: opened (path), in, next.

printer_add.description: Keep a printer on the network by name (1 to 40 characters): kind octoprint (key: its API key, required), moonraker or klipper (key only if it asks for one), prusalink (key, or user and password for its digest login); url its address (http:// is assumed). Kept in .agentlink-printers.json in the session's folder; the key and password are never given back by any tool. The same name again replaces it. It is tried at once (check: false skips that): reached true with state, or reached false with why — it is kept either way. Bambu Lab printers are refused: they take jobs only over their own LAN protocol or from Bambu Studio (slice_with { slicer: "bambustudio" }, then send from there). Never ask the person to paste a key into a chat they do not trust; a key is theirs to give. Reply: added { name, kind, url, how it logs in }, replaced, kept (the file), reached, state | why. Changes nothing in the document.

printer_list.description: The printers kept by printer_add: printers [{ name, kind, url, how it logs in }] — never the keys. remove: a name forgets that printer (refused when it is not kept, listing those that are) and the reply adds removed. Changes nothing in the document.

printer_status.description: A printer's state now, asked over the network: printer (its name from printer_add; may be left out when one is kept). Reply: printer, kind, state (the printer's own word: idle, printing, paused, error …), nozzle { now, target } and bed { now, target } °C, job { file, progress % , and time left or printed where the printer gives it }. Refused when no printer is kept, the name is not kept, or the printer does not answer (its address, key, or it is off). Changes nothing.

printer_send.description: Upload a G-code file to a printer: file (required) an absolute path or a name in the session's folder (.gcode, .gco, .g, .bgcode — slice and slice_with write it); printer may be left out when one is kept; storage: where on the printer (local for OctoPrint, gcodes for Moonraker, usb for PrusaLink when left out). It is uploaded and NOT started. Starting needs both start: true and confirm: "start <printer name>" word for word, and that is the person's call: ask them first, never start a print on your own. With start it is refused while the printer is printing, paused or busy. Reply: uploaded, where, started, printer, bytes, note.

printer_pause.description: Pause the printer's running job. confirm (required): "pause <printer name>" word for word — the person's call: ask them first. printer may be left out when one is kept. Refused without the exact confirm, or when the printer does not answer. Reply: printer and what the printer answered.

printer_stop.description: Stop (cancel) the printer's job; it cannot be resumed and the print is lost. confirm (required): "stop <printer name>" word for word — the person's call: ask them first, every time. printer may be left out when one is kept. Refused without the exact confirm, or when the printer does not answer. Reply: printer and what the printer answered.

cut_check.description: Can a body in a cut setup be cut from sheet. It must be a sheet part: two parallel flat faces a constant thickness apart and every other face square to them (the faces that are not are named under sheet.notSquare and sheet.steps). Then, for the machine (laser, waterjet, plasma, router), material and thickness: its thickness against the setup's sheet; holes, webs (material left between cuts) and slots under the least feature; a router's inside corners tighter than its cutter; plasma holes under the thickness; the part against the sheet [w, h]. machine, material and sheet given here override the cut setup's for this check. Materials: steel, stainless, aluminium, brass, copper, titanium, acrylic, plywood, wood, mdf, hdpe, polycarbonate, cardboard, rubber, foam, carbon (steel is assumed, plywood on a router, when neither says). Refused when the body is in no cut setup (setup add { type: "cut" } first) or has no flat face. Reply: body, verdict (fix | pass with warnings | pass), machine, material, kerf, sheet { thickness, normal }, profile { size [x, y], holes, edges, leastWeb, leastGap }, least (the limits used), findings [{ rule (not-sheet, thickness, small-hole, thin-web, narrow-slot, inside-corner, sheet-size), severity, value, limit, at, says }] (the first 10), setup, unjudged (sheet size when no sheet is given), assumed (what the setup left out: machine laser, material, kerf, thickness), note. The least features are rules of thumb; the cutting shop's own figures win. Webs are not read on a profile of over 160 edges (assumed says so). Changes nothing.

cut_export.description: Write the flat profiles of sheet bodies as DXF and SVG in mm, laid out on a sheet, to the session's folder. body, or bodies [names] (the one body when left out), each in a cut setup; copies: n, or { "body label": n } (1 to 500); sheet [w, h] (the cut setup's when left out); gap mm between parts and from the edge (3 mm or two kerfs); formats ["dxf", "svg"] (both when left out); name: the files' base name. With a sheet the parts are placed by FreeCAD's BIM nesting (Arch_Nest's module, parts never turned); nest: false, no sheet, or BIM not there lays them in rows instead — layout says which and why. Parts that do not fit are counted under left. compensate: true offsets each outline out and each hole in by half the kerf; leave it off when the cutter's software does that. DXF is R12 (LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, POLYLINE) on layers OUTER and HOLES; each file is read back and counted (readBack, matches). One thickness per file: bodies of another thickness are refused. Refused too when a body is not a sheet part (cut_check says why) or nothing fits the sheet. Nesting many copies of an intricate outline can take a minute or more: export fewer copies per call. Reply: files { dxf { path, bytes, readBack, layers, matches }, svg { path, bytes, readBack } }, placed { body: n }, left, sheet, thickness, kerf, compensated, gap, entities, layout, note. Writes files only; the document is not changed.

mill_check.description: Can a body in a mill setup be milled: faces no tool direction reaches (undercuts, named), faces past the tool's reach, inside corners tighter than the least tool can leave, holes and pockets past the reach or over 4 times as deep as wide, walls too thin for the material, and the stock. directions: the sides the tool comes from ("+z", "-x" …); left out, the setup's axes ("3": +z only; "3+2": all six). tool: the least end mill's diameter mm (the setup's minTool, else 3); reach mm (5 x tool or 20); material aluminium, steel, stainless, brass, copper, titanium, plastic, pom, wood (aluminium when left out); stock [x, y, z] mm as the part stands (the part's box + 2 mm a side and 1 mm top and bottom when left out). Refused when the body is in no mill setup (setup add { type: "mill" } first). Reply: body, verdict (fix | pass with warnings | pass), directions, tool, reach, material, stock, findings [{ rule, severity, says, faces }] (the first 10), leastWall, setup, grade, assumed (every value the setup or the call left out, in words). Trap: a face on the stock's outside counts as the stock's own; faces are sampled, so a small undercut between samples can be missed. Face names change after any edit. Changes nothing; heavy on bodies with many faces.

mill_export.description: Write a milled body's STEP file (read back and compared) and its setup sheet to the session's folder; takes mill_check's inputs (directions, tool, reach, material, stock) and runs that check first. name: the files' base name. With FreeCAD's CAM (cam: true, the default): the CAM Job that already holds the body is reused as it is; else a NEW Job is added to the document with a box stock and the least tool used here — this changes the document (a Job, its stock, model clone and tool controller; one undo step) — and CAM's own Sanity report (HTML) is the setup sheet, with Make's mill check added to it (verdict, findings, least wall, what was assumed). A new Job has no operations: add them with the cam_ tools. The window is left as it was: CAM's Sanity report hides every object to take its pictures and puts back only part of them, so each object of the document is shown or hidden again as before the call (camJob.shownAgain: how many were put back), and a new Job's box stock and tool model are hidden, as CAM's own Job leaves them (the stock shows with CAM's job tools). cam: false, or CAM failing, writes Make's own Markdown sheet instead and camNote says why; nothing is added to the document then. Refused when the body is in no mill setup. Reply: body, verdict, step { path, bytes, volumeDiff (mm³ between the STEP read back and the body), solids }, findings (how many), setupSheet { path, bytes, by }, camJob { label, reused, note, shownAgain }, camNote. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

fea_frame.description: A frame of straight members solved with beam elements (CalculiX B32) — beams, rafters, portal frames, trusses, shelving. A sizing look, not a sign-off: joints are rigid and connections are not designed. members [{ name, from [x, y, z], to [x, y, z] mm, section { kind rect (b, d) | circ (d) | pipe (d, t) | box (b, d, t) } mm, material }], or bodies [labels]: box-like members whose centre line and width and depth are read from their shape (rect sections; the larger of the two cross sizes is taken as depth for an upright member). material: an id from material_list for all members (or per member); it must have a Young's modulus. supports (required) [{ at [x, y, z] a member's end, kind pinned | fixed | roller }] — at must be within tolerance mm of an end (1, or the largest section size with bodies). loads [{ member, w: N/mm downward (or [wx, wy, wz]) } | { member, kPa, width mm (1000) } | { at [x, y, z] a joint, force [fx, fy, fz] N }]; gravity: true adds own weight (−z). elements per member (8); deflectionLimit (e.g. 360) judges span over deflection; timeout s (300); name names the study's folder. Refused: CalculiX (ccx) not found (set its path in FEM's preferences or AGENTLINK_CCX); no members; no supports; an unknown section kind or material; a member end that is not [x, y, z]. Runs as a job (seconds for a small frame; job_status finishes a longer one). Changes nothing in the document: the input deck and results are files in the session's folder. Reply: members [{ member, length, axialBendingMPa [min, max], vonMisesMPa, safety (yield over von Mises, where the material has a yield), deflectionMm (across the member, from the line between its ends), spanOverDeflection, deflectionOk, movesMm }], supports [{ at, kind, reactionN }], loadTotalN, loadN (its size, one number), reactionsNote (when CalculiX reads the reactions short of the load), files (the study's folder), worst (the member with the least safety), verdict (a few words: "least safety 2.4, Rafter", "past yield: safety 0.8, Post" below 1, or the largest stress where no material gives a yield), bodies (the labels of the bodies it was made from, when given), elements, note. More: guide_read { topic: "frame" }.

gen_make.description: Make a Gridfinity bin to size as a new body (open Gridfinity profile, 42 mm cells, 7 mm height units), centred on the origin in X and Y and standing on z = 0, or put 10 mm clear beside (+X of) what the document already holds. generator: gridfinity_bin (the only one here; gen_part makes baseplates and boxes). name: the body's label (left out: "Gridfinity bin 2x1x4" style; a second of the same gets " 2"). params {  …  }. Counts are whole numbers, sizes mm; an unknown key or a value out of range is refused with the keys or the range. measure: true builds it and answers the sizes without adding anything (made: false). The body is a plain Part solid (Part::Feature), not a PartDesign Body: hw_embed, mass_ballast and the part_ tools work on it directly; it has no feature history to edit — make it again with other params instead. It takes a second or two; bins of many cells with dividers a little longer. magnets: true leaves four 6 x 2 mm holes under each cell, open to the bed: press them in after printing, or drop them in at the pause — encased { what, pauseAt mm, note } gives the height, hw_pauses lists it once the bin is in a print setup, and slice writes the pause. Reply: generator, values (every parameter as used, defaults filled in), parts [{ name, volume mm³, min, max, size }], bodies [labels], sound { label: true|false }, printerFit (the calibration the holes took), movedBy (when it was put beside what is already there), step, kind (the generator in words) and measured (the first piece's size in words, "83.5 x 41.5 x 32.4 mm", and a lid when there is one); with measure: true, made: false and no bodies, encased. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

gen_part.description: Make a standard part to size, each piece its own new body (a box and its lid are two; the lid is laid beside the box, printed top down — turn it over about X to put it on). generator (required): gridfinity_baseplate (42 mm pockets; style open, or magnets: a floor with four 6 x 2 holes a pocket), project_box (a box and lid; bosses: corner screw bosses with pilot holes and clearance holes in the lid), board_box (an enclosure round a circuit board: standoffs under its mounting holes, connector openings, a lid; for a KiCad board, board_enclosure reads all that from the import instead). name: the body's label (the lid gets " lid" after it). Holes take the printer's fit calibration kept with the document (fit calibrate); without one they are made 0.2 mm big and printerFit says so. measure: true builds it and answers the sizes without adding anything (made: false). The parts go at the origin in an empty document, else 10 mm clear beside (+X of) what is there (movedBy). They are plain Part solids (Part::Feature), no feature history: make it again with other params to change it. A wrong generator, an unknown key or a value out of range is refused with what is allowed. Params —  … . Reply: generator, values (every parameter as used, defaults filled in), parts [{ name, volume mm³, min, max, size }], bodies [labels], sound { label: true|false }, printerFit (the calibration the holes took), movedBy (when it was put beside what is already there), step, kind (the generator in words) and measured (the first piece's size in words, "83.5 x 41.5 x 32.4 mm", and a lid when there is one); with measure: true, made: false and no bodies, and what the generator says of what it made: outside and inside [x, y, z], lid { plate, lip, clearance, at, note }, bosses or standoffs { screw, at, pilot, pilotDepth … }, boardAt, openings, and for a baseplate pockets (how many), height and magnets. A changing call's reply may also carry health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

history_checkpoint.description: Save a copy of the document now (name: optional; named ones are kept), to come back to with history_restore or measure from with history_diff { since } — past FreeCAD's 20-step undo and across restarts. list: true lists this document's checkpoints. The person's file is never touched.

history_restore.description: Go back to a checkpoint (its id, cp3, or its name): by undo while the stack reaches it, else by reopening its saved copy (the state before is checkpointed first, so a restore can be undone the same way).

macro_save.description: Save this session's changing calls as a FreeCAD macro (.FCMacro in the person's macro folder): name, from / to (a checkpoint or step; the whole session by default), params { wall: 2.0, length: 60 } — the key sizes, named at the top of the macro and put in place of each value in the calls. It runs (macro_run) only once the person approves it.

macro_list.description: The macros in FreeCAD's macro folder (what Macro › Macros… lists: .FCMacro and .py), each approved, changed (its code moved since the OK) or not approved. Changes nothing.

macro_show.description: One macro's text, its named sizes and how many calls it makes, and whether it is approved. Changes nothing.

macro_approve.description: The person approves a macro to be run by Agent Link: confirm: "approve <name>" typed by them, never by the agent — a macro is Python with the Mac's full reach. Approval holds until its file changes.

macro_unapprove.description: Take a macro off the approved list.

macro_run.description: Run an approved macro as FreeCAD's Macro dialog runs it: params { CONSTANT: value } changes its named sizes for this run. One checkpoint before; a failure part way rolls the whole run back. An unapproved or changed macro is refused.

app_recover.description: Documents back after a crash or a hang: action list (each document's saved copies: auto-saves, checkpoints, FreeCAD's recovery files; the document with the newest copy first; a recovered copy listed only with changes of its own) | auto { documents [{ name, label, file }], since } (the documents open at the crash only: the newest copy of each that opens, beside the file as "<label> (recovered HH:MM)"; one per original, a recovered copy never recovered again beside it; a recovered copy that was open comes back only from changes made in it after it opened, and one with none (or modified: false) is named in notRecoveredAgain — never a copy of a copy; a person's saved file that was unchanged at the crash (file given, modified false or not said) is not recovered: it opens again from its own file as itself, once — left alone when it is open already — and is named in reopened; it comes back from a copy only when a copy newer than its file holds more or the file will not open; temporary recovered copies older than the crash (since) that FreeCAD opened again unchanged are closed; copies opened are marked unchanged, so they are not read as changed or recovered again) | accept { document, confirm: "save over <file name>" typed by the person } (the recovered copy saved over their file, the old one kept).

pref_history.description: The settings changes Agent Link made, newest first: change number, time, tool, path, name, from, to, and whether a restart is needed (limit, 20 by default). Changes nothing.

pref_rollback.description: Put FreeCAD's settings back as they were before a change (to: its number from pref_history, or a time YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS): the whole settings file from its snapshot, written while FreeCAD is down — the window restarts around it in the background (save as app_restart's); the state before is snapshotted too.
